title: What If One Dam Could Slow Down the Whole Planet?

scenes.text: What if one dam could slow the whole planet's spin? A NASA scientist calculated that one does.
China's Three Gorges Dam holds about 40 cubic kilometers of water, roughly 10 trillion gallons, high above sea level.
That mass sits farther from Earth's axis, like a skater stretching out her arms, so the planet spins a little slower.
Geophysicist Benjamin Fong Chao worked out the cost: each day gets about 0.06 microseconds longer.
That is six hundredths of a millionth of a second. The 2004 Indonesian quake shortened the day by 2.68 microseconds, about 45 times more.
So you will never notice it. But humans moved enough water to change how fast a planet turns.
